subject: plot of fhets and mhets in gl.report.sexlinked

messages.author: 0bfeefd4d077b98c
messages.subject: plot of fhets and mhets in gl.report.sexlinked
parts:
Hi there,

Thanks for the new version of dartR!

I have been working with gl.report.sexlinked and am unsure what is happening within the function. When I get the plot of female vs male heterozygosity of my loci after sex linked loci have been removed, it looks as I would expect it too (i.e. all loci are ~<0.5). 

What I want is a list of all loci, and their genotype frequencies. My understanding is that if I set t.het and t.hom = 1, then it will return all loci. 

However, when I look at df$zzzw many loci have fhet and/or mhet >0.5, i.e. this is not what is being plotted. I cannot work out where the plot is getting the data from. Why is the data in the report different to what is being plotted? How can I access the fhet and mhet data that has been plotted?

Hope that makes sense! Thanks!
Lana

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: plot of fhets and mhets in gl.report.sexlinked
parts:
Hi Lana,

Thank you for reporting that bug. Now the information in the report and in the plot is the same. You can use the updated version of this function by installing the beta version of dartR by typing in the R console:

>  library(dartR)
> gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "beta")

Cheers,
Luis

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: plot of fhets and mhets in gl.report.sexlinked
parts:
Hi Lana,

There was a bug in the installation function gl.install.vanilla.dartR(). I fixed this bug. Please use the following code to install the updated version:

 devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR",
                                     ref = "beta,
                                     dependencies = TRUE)

Cheers,
Luis
